idiom_name: asynchronous queue handoff instead of a blocking wait (no main-thread suspension)
implementation_notes: JavaScript cannot park the main thread: a realm runs one thread and Atomics.wait throws when the calling thread cannot be blocked (MDN), so a monitor-style guarded suspension would freeze the timers, I/O callbacks and promise reactions that were supposed to signal it. The idiom is therefore suspension of the task rather than of the thread - an async function awaits a promise, async iterator or queue entry that the producer resolves when the condition becomes true, which is the same guard expressed with Async Method Invocation (the awaited item is the evidence that the condition holds). A literal predicate wait exists only inside worker threads, where Atomics.wait/waitAsync over a SharedArrayBuffer coordinates with Atomics.notify; use that for worker-pool internals and never as the application's coordination mechanism.
pitfalls: A blocking substitute (spin, sleep loop, Atomics.wait on the main thread) stops the event loop, so the notifier can never run and the program deadlocks instead of waiting.
Atomics.wait requires a SharedArrayBuffer and a worker thread, and browsers only expose SharedArrayBuffer under cross-origin isolation.
An awaited handoff is not a monitor: another task can consume the value between resolve and resume, so the condition must be re-checked after every await.
alternative: Await an asynchronous queue or deferred that the producer resolves when the condition holds (Async Method Invocation, e.g. an async queue/async iterable), reserving Atomics.wait/waitAsync over a SharedArrayBuffer for coordination inside worker threads.
